messages:
zoe: Heads-up  offer for a candidate starting 12/20. Managers asking if the year-end company holiday (12/24-1/1) will consume their PTO or if they're paid holiday time.
lina: If they're on payroll on 12/24 they get the paid shutdown days like other FTEs. PTO accruals are pro-rated from 12/20. Carryover eligibility requires being employed on 12/31.
mark: So if they start 12/20 and remain active on 12/31 theyll be eligible to carry within cap? Managers worried about using days during onboarding week.
hr-bot: Policy snippet: "Employees on payroll for the shutdown period receive paid company holiday per status. New hires accrue PTO pro-rata; carryover eligibility is based on active employee status on Dec 31. Blackout windows restrict scheduling but do not change accrual/carryover rules."
zoe: Nice. Another ask: should offer letters mention they won't be required to use PTO for company shutdown if they start before it? What wording is safest?
lina: Suggested line: "If your start date is before the company holiday shutdown, you will be paid for company-observed holidays and will not be required to use PTO for those days." Keep it short and refer to the employee handbook link.
mark: Can payroll confirm proration formula so compops can include exact days in offer?
payroll-bot: FYI: proration = (days active in pay period / total pay period days) * standard accrual. For shutdown holiday pay, check hire date < shutdown start to qualify. Submit payroll ticket for edge cases.
zoe: Thanks all  I'll add that sentence to the offer template and link to the handbook. Closing the loop. :thumbsup:
